For those unfamiliar with Greek gods (if anyone happens to read this at all ^^;) My main man Apollo is the Greek god of several things not least music, art, plague, prophecies and much more. He also happens to be one of a twin, too! (his sister's name is Artemis) But that is another story. Today, since this sub is really empty, I thought I'd share one of my personal favourite Greek stories and it is that of Apollo and one of his many human lovers, Hyacinthus. That is, Hyacinthus, the youth, not Hyacinth, the flower but you'll understand the relation in a moment~

First, we must begin with Hyacinthus (or sometimes Hyacinth) who was a handsome Spartan prince. Athletic and able, he caught the eye of the god Apollo who fell in love with the youth and so started a love affair with him. However, if his beauty was enough to attract one god, it surely attracted others but none more than Zephyrus, the west wind. Thus, a feud began between Apollo and Zephyrus over Hyacinthus. In either case, Apollo and Hyacinthus would often play games together (if you know what I mean) including throwing the discus. They would take turned throwing it one after the other when after a while Hyacinthus took it to himself to impress his lover by running out to catch the discus Apollo threw.

Now, if you have any knowledge of mythology then you won't be surprised when I tell you that there are countless variations on most tales. In this case, there are two major versions of the ending that I know of so I'll give them to you one after the other in no particular order. The first is that in running out to catch the disc, Hyacinthus made a very naive decision and was struck across the head and fell on the spot. The second, however, has us believe that Zephyrus, consumed with jealousy, blew the discus just so much off course as that it would strike the youth dead. In either case, Apollo, in guilt and in grief, refused to let Hades take his young lover so changed the boy's body into that of a hyacinth, the pretty purple flower we know today. Ovid adds that Apollo's falling tears stained the petals and so, we are given a fine etiological story for the origin of Hyacinths~

I hope you enjoyed that! I'm kind of new to these kinds of websites so if there is something I messed up on or could have added, let me know and I'll make an edit~ (^^)
